Name: Ignatius of Antioch
Summary: Bishop of Antioch who was taken to Rome under guard to be martyred in the early second century, writing letters to churches along the way.
Contribution: His seven letters stressed the unity of the local church around its bishop, the reality of Christ's incarnation and suffering, and faithful endurance under persecution, giving an early window into church order and devotion to Christ.
KeyWorks: Seven Letters (to the Ephesians, Magnesians, Trallians, Romans, Philadelphians, Smyrnaeans, and to Polycarp)
Testimony: Wrote as a condemned prisoner on his way to death in Rome, urging the churches to stay united and to follow Christ even to martyrdom.
